Vehicle & cross-variable insights

Top 3 highest-impact findings, Jan–Jun 2026
1Overnight arrivals take 2.2× longer to unload
~1,247 hrs
Estimated potential time saved
The 12AM–6AM arrival window averages 327.2 min per unload — more than double the 151.1 min average for the very next window, 6AM–9AM. This isn't a one-off: it holds across all seven days of the week. Shifting a portion of overnight arrivals into the early-morning window is the single biggest scheduling lever in the data.
  • Current 12AM–6AM job count 1,416 jobs
  • % of jobs considered for shifting 30%
  • Jobs affected ≈425 jobs
  • Current avg unloading time 327.2 min
  • Alt. (6AM–9AM) avg unloading time 151.1 min
  • Est. time saved ≈74,800 min (~1,247 hrs)
214.5 FT - Cage: highest volume, 76% over KPI
~1,961 hrs
Estimated potential time saved
The 14.5 FT - CAGE is the fleet's highest-volume vehicle type at 2,575 jobs, but averages 105.7 min per unload against a 60 min KPI target — 45.7 min (76%) over target on every single job. Because of its volume, this is the largest cumulative efficiency gap of any vehicle type in the fleet, well ahead of lower-volume types with bigger per-job overages.
  • Current job count 2,575 jobs
  • Current avg unloading time 105.7 min
  • KPI target 60 min
  • Overage per job +45.7 min (76%)
  • Est. time saved if brought to KPI ≈117,700 min (~1,961 hrs)
3Morning peak (6AM–9AM) is overloaded vs. off-peak
~847 hrs
Estimated potential time saved
6AM–9AM handles more job volume than any other time band — 4,180 jobs — and averages 151.1 min per unload, versus just 90.3 min in the quieter 3PM–6PM window (2,541 jobs). The combination of high volume and high unloading time makes the morning peak the biggest congestion point on the schedule; rebalancing some of that volume toward the afternoon lull would relieve it.
  • Current 6AM–9AM job count 4,180 jobs
  • % of jobs considered for shifting 20%
  • Jobs affected ≈836 jobs
  • Current avg unloading time 151.1 min
  • Alt. (3PM–6PM) avg unloading time 90.3 min
  • Est. time saved ≈50,800 min (~847 hrs)
How to read this: Unloading-time averages exclude outlet visits with a negative or missing arrival/departure scan (per the data-quality note below) but those visits still count toward job volume. "Estimated time saved" figures are potential, directional savings based on the observed gap between time bands or against KPI — they assume shifted jobs perform at the target band's or KPI's average, which is not guaranteed, and should be treated as a planning input rather than a committed number.
